title: Sources, Subject B

reference.grammar: The sources Subject B was drawn from.

techniques.name: Orthographic set

ground.label: Ground
ground.note: What the figure is drawn on: a blank sheet or ruled graph paper.

pitch.label: Grid pitch
pitch.note: Graph-paper square, in figure units. Acts with Ground on Graph paper.

sec.label: Section
sec.note: How a cut wall is filled: section lining, or solid black, the drafting convention for a thin wall.

sgap.label: Lining spacing
sgap.note: Distance between the section lines, in figure units, at the drafting standard of 45°. Acts with Section on Hatched.

weight.label: Line weight
weight.note: Every stroke of the figure at this multiple of its measured width.

hand.label: Hand
hand.note: How far a line may wander from its ruled path, in figure units: 0 is drawn with instruments, higher is a freehand drawing of the same object, in long gentle strokes.

dash.label: Dash length
dash.note: The dashes and gaps of every dashed line, as a multiple of the measured pattern.

type.label: Type size
type.note: Every label at this multiple of its measured size, from its own anchor. Held to the range where no label meets a line or the edge of the sheet.

techniques.implementation: A subject drawn front, side and top in thin line, with its sources beside it. The geometry is measured from the source figure; the engine redraws it, and each dial is a decision of the drawing that the figure has: ground, line weight, hand, box corners, dashes, nodes, arrowheads, tone and the setting of the labels.

techniques.name: Measured inks
techniques.implementation: solid ink pixels of each figure, read at full resolution, are clustered to five colors; a color is kept when it holds at least 4% of the ink.

techniques.name: Figure and ground
techniques.implementation: The ground is the most common border color of a figure; ink is every pixel more than 40 levels from it.

techniques.name: Justified plate
techniques.implementation: Figures keep their proportions and share a row height; each row fills the plate width. Every split of the figures into rows is tried, and the one whose row heights sit closest to the target wins.

pass_order: line · every stroke, ruled or by hand
